title: COMET: Learning Cardinality Constrained Mixture of Experts with Trees and Local Search

problem.claim: Sparse expert selection can produce convergence, performance, and low-quality-solution problems when trained with first-order optimization methods.

gap.claim: Existing sparse gates and first-order training methods do not adequately address the optimization challenges of cardinality-constrained expert selection.

contributions.claim: COMET is a differentiable sparse gate based on a tree mechanism for mixture-of-experts models.
A permutation-based local-search method complements first-order training for sparse gates, including Hash routing, Top-k, DSelect-k, and COMET.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present COMET as a new sparse gate with a novel tree-based mechanism and the local-search procedure as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that COMET outperforms state-of-the-art gates.
On standard vision and recommender-system benchmarks, COMET+ achieves up to 13% ROC AUC improvement over Hash routing and Top-k, and up to 9% over DSelect-k.
Local search combined with Top-k and Hash gates reportedly reduces the hyperparameter-tuning budget by up to 100X, and the approach improves over MoEBERT on 5 of 7 GLUE benchmarks and SQuAD.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sparse mixture-of-experts models scale capacity by selecting a subset of experts for each input.
Existing sparse gates and first-order optimization can suffer from convergence, performance, and solution-quality issues.
The paper introduces the COMET sparse gate and a permutation-based local-search method.
The methods are evaluated across recommender systems, vision, and natural language processing.
The authors report gains in ROC AUC, hyperparameter-tuning efficiency, and language-modeling benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: A differentiable tree-based sparse gate is reported to improve performance while exploiting sparse computation.

interpretation.claim: The routing structure may jointly affect optimization behavior and computational efficiency.

application.claim: When designing sparse expert routers, evaluate both differentiability and the computational structure of the routing mechanism.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these benefits hold across architectures, datasets, or training settings beyond those evaluated.

source_observation.claim: Permutation-based local search is reported to help sparse-gate training escape bad initializations or solutions.

interpretation.claim: Combining first-order optimization with targeted combinatorial search may mitigate local optimization failures.

application.claim: For discrete or combinatorial routing decisions, consider local search as a complement to gradient-based training.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the computational overhead, stopping criteria, or cases where local search fails to help.

unknowns: Exact model architectures, datasets, splits, and training configurations are unspecified.
The computational overhead and implementation details of COMET and local search are unspecified.
Statistical uncertainty and the conditions behind the reported maximum improvements are unspecified.
